items.article_search_text: Alpine's Pierre Gasly delivered one of the best, most surprisingly good qualifying performances this season. Pierre Gaslyyyyyyy (in Daniel Ricciardo and Yuki Tsunoda's voices)! Saturday's qualifying session at Monza delivered the goods, and Alpine's Pierre Gasly is right in the center of it. In contrast, two of the favorites, Ferrari and McLaren, underwhelmed at the Temple of Speed [https://roundtable.io/sports/f1/news/why-monza-is-f1-s-temple-of-speed-and-the-circuit-that-made-history]. REDEMPTION FOR THE FRENCHMAN This week has been a rollercoaster of emotions for Alpine driver Pierre Gasly. Before the weekend, he received news that his penalties at Monaco [https://sports.yahoo.com/articles/f1-championship-standings-monaco-gp-123529877.html] were reinstated, stripping him of a podium finish. As a result, Alpine took a hit in the Teams' Standings, dropping to 54 points. That's a big hit in their midfield race against the Racing Bulls. But Gasly put his head down and went to work on Saturday. Alpine clearly got the setup on their car right, with both of their drivers advancing to Q3. Then, with George Russell setting the provisional fastest time, Gasly sped down the asphalt and snatched pole [https://roundtable.io/sports/f1/news/pierre-gasly-stuns-monza-to-claim-historic-italian-grand-prix-pole-position] by a mere .060 advantage. This was Gasly's first pole position in Formula One, and it was a feat that he will never forget. PIASTRI'S PROMISING SATURDAY UNRAVELS Finally, it looked like Oscar Piastri was about to outperform McLaren teammate Lando Norris. Norris has won the last two races, adding more motivation for the Australian driver to do better this weekend. In the running for pole in Q3, Piastri would botch his final fast lap, locking up and exceeding track limits early in the lap. He had to settle for a third-place start, but not for long. Piastri incurred a three-place grid penalty for impeding Red Bull driver Liam Lawson in Q2. He will start sixth on Sunday, two spots ahead of Norris. SO MUCH FOR THE HOME TEAM'S UPGRADES Most of the people in the grandstand left dissatisfied, as Ferrari clearly lacked the pace to fight for pole position. Heading into this weekend, the home team stirred up hype with a newly upgraded power unit and a revised floor board, only for Charles Leclerc to qualify P4 and Lewis Hamilton P5. The Piastri penalty bumped both drivers to P3 and P4, but it was still a disappointing Saturday for the Prancing Horse. RED BULL DRIVER MIGHT MISS THIRD CONSECUTIVE RACE Due to a wrist injury, Red Bull driver Isack Hadjar is sitting out his second straight race weekend at Monza. Rumors have it that Hadjar will also miss the Spanish Grand Prix next week, as he's still recovering from his injury. Red Bull team principal Laurent Mekies said that it will be "difficult" for Hadjar to return to action at the Madring race, which is scheduled for September 11-13.

items.article_search_text: A rival driver was fuming at the Australian star after the blunder and he made his thoughts known. 7NEWS brings you the latest local news from Australia and around the world. Stay up to date with all of the breaking sport, politics, entertainment, finance, weather and business headlines. Today's news, live updates & all the latest breaking stories from 7NEWS. McLaren’s Oscar Piastri qualified third at the ‘Temple of Speed’ but was then handed a three-place penalty at the Italian Grand Prix for impeding Red Bull’s Liam Lawson. It was a big blow for the Australian as Pierre Gasly delivered the shock of the season by taking the first pole position of his career for Sunday’s race. Piastri slowed to allow Lawson’s teammate Max Verstappen through but delayed the New Zealander — a Red Bull substitute — when he slotted in ahead of him at the first chicane during the closing stages of Q2. “Dude, what the f***,” Lawson could be heard saying immediately after the incident. After hearing from both drivers, Red Bull and McLaren team representatives, and reviewing the range of data available to them, the stewarding panel settled on a grid drop for the Australian. That meant Piastri — currently seventh in the standings — fell from third to sixth on the grid, promoting Ferrari pair Charles Leclerc and Lewis Hamilton, as well as the Red Bull of Lawson’s team mate, Max. George Russell, widely expected to claim a much-needed pole in his world championship quest, had to settle for second on Saturday, pipped to top spot by Gasly by just 0.060 seconds. Speaking before the penalty was applied, Piastri said: “It was a tricky situation to manage. I was coming out of the pits and got told that Lawson and Verstappen were coming, but I kind of had to jump on the brakes pretty heavily to get out of Max’s way, and then I was just stuck in a very awkward spot with Liam.” Piastri added: “The speed difference coming out of the pits is so big here, so I don’t really know where he came from.” Gasly’s improbable triumph arrived a day on from his Alpine boss Flavio Briatore accusing an FIA judge of having a “working relationship” with McLaren after the British team’s appeal led to the Frenchman being stripped of his podium from June’s Monaco Grand Prix. Championship leader Kimi Antonelli took seventh but will start his home race from the back of the grid as he serves an engine penalty. World champion Lando Norris arrived in Italy with consecutive victories under his belt but looks almost certain to miss out on a hat-trick after he could manage only ninth. With Antonelli starting Sunday’s 53-lap race from the rear, Russell knew this event would hand him a golden chance to eat into his Mercedes teammate’s 59-point championship lead. But the Englishman will have to see off Gasly’s unexpected challenge to claim a full quota of points in what could prove a pivotal contest in the title race with 11 rounds still to go. Hamilton spoke about his dream of winning in Monza for a record sixth time and a first for Ferrari in the build-up to the Italian team’s home event. But the seven-time world champion endured a difficult afternoon. At one stage, Hamilton’s presence in Q3 appeared in grave danger after he could set only the 10th quickest time. However, his blushes were spared by just one- thousandth of a second. It was an unsatisfactory afternoon for Red Bull with Verstappen – who claimed his car was “broken” and “undriveable” – three-tenths off the pace. But there were no such concerns for Gasly as he flourished in his Alpine. “I have been waiting for that one,” yelled the Frenchman – whose sole victory of his Formula One life arrived in Monza six years ago – over the radio. Fernando Alonso qualified 21st, with only Aston Martin teammate Lance Stroll slower. Journalist from the 7NEWS.com.au team.

Oscar Piastri has been awarded a three-place grid penalty for impeding Liam Lawson during qualifying for the Formula 1 Italian Grand Prix. Piastri put early qualifying struggles aside to put his McLaren third on the grid for Sunday's race, but concern was raised in Q3 he could be in hot water with the stewards after an incident with Liam Lawson. Lawson, starting his final Q2 run, had ventured onto the track before the rest of the field with Max Verstappen to ensure he had a tow on his lap, vital on Monza's long straights, But the New Zealander's hopes were dashed as he approached Turn 1, entering the corner as Piastri joined the circuit, blocking Lawson's line and forcing him to slow down, Lawson was eliminated at the chequered flag. The stewards noted the incident before opening an investigation. Their decision was to penalise Piastri, stripping him of third place by imposing a three-place grid penalty. In their rationale, the stewards explained that Piastri stated he was not aware of Verstappen and Lawson's push laps, so took no avoiding action. Read full stewards decision bel ow "The Stewards heard from the driver of Car 81 (Oscar Piastri), the driver of Car 30 (Liam Lawson), team representatives and reviewed positioning/marshalling system data, video, timing, telemetry, team radio and in-car video evidence. "On leaving the pits, the driver of Car 81 was advised that “Verstappen, Lawson and Sainz just crossing, Sainz has pitted, Just Verstappen and Lawson, watch out for them as you join”. The driver of Car 81 stated that he was not alerted to the fact that VER and LAW were on push laps but realised as he was almost at turn 1 that VER was on a push lap. He slowed significantly and kept to the right to allow VER to pass but was unable to do anything to avoid impeding LAW who was close behind. "The Stewards accept that with the information he had, and the situation he was placed in, the driver of Car 81 had, at this stage, no other options available and hence, inadvertently, and also unnecessarily, impeded Car 30. Therefore the standard penalty of a drop of 3 grid positions is imposed." READ MORE: Pierre Gasly takes shock pole position for F1 Italian GP

On the circuit where he famously claimed his maiden Grand Prix victory in 2020, Gasly produced a remarkable final Q3 lap of 1m21.786s to snatch top spot by just 0.060s from Russell. Piastri was a further 0.120s back in third, while the entire top 10 was covered by only half a second. The result marked a memorable afternoon for Alpine, with Gasly consistently featuring at the sharp end throughout the session and team mate Franco Colapinto also making it through to the pole position shoot-out. When Q1 got under way, several drivers were already facing difficult Sundays ahead, with Kimi Antonelli, Alexander Albon and Liam Lawson set to take grid penalties following power unit changes. The opening runs brought an early benchmark from Verstappen, before the Ferraris and McLarens joined the action. However, it was Gasly who soon made his presence felt, the Alpine driver setting a 1m22.612s to move to the top of the timesheets. Colapinto also impressed as Alpine's strong pace became increasingly clear, while Antonelli and Russell moved into the top five. Russell notably completed his early effort on medium tyres rather than the soft compound. As the session entered its closing stages, the battle to escape elimination intensified. Gasly's earlier lap proved good enough to remain fastest, ahead of Verstappen, Norris, Colapinto and an impressive Lindblad. There were concerns, however, at McLaren. Norris reported significant difficulties under braking, particularly into the first chicane, while Piastri also experienced similar problems on his way through the opening segment. At the other end of the order, Tsunoda was eliminated in 17th, having struggled to put together a clean lap. Albon also exited, along with the Cadillac pairing of Bottas and Perez and the Aston Martin duo of Alonso and Stroll. Q2 brought further drama, with Red Bull among the first teams to send their drivers out. Verstappen set an early benchmark but quickly reported problems with the rear of his car, describing it as difficult to drive through several of Monza's key corners. Once the rest of the field had completed their initial attempts, Piastri led the way with Norris close behind and Gasly again firmly in contention. Russell and Antonelli followed, while Hamilton found himself outside the top 10 and facing a nervous final run. The Ferrari driver responded under pressure. With just one opportunity remaining to secure his place in Q3, Hamilton improved sufficiently to progress – but only by the narrowest of margins. The seven-time World Champion ultimately edged Audi's Gabriel Bortoleto by just 0.001s, with the Brazilian therefore missing out on a place in the final segment. Bearman, Hulkenberg, Lawson, Sainz and Ocon were also eliminated. Antonelli topped Q2 with a lap of 1m21.882s, ahead of the McLaren pair, Gasly and Russell, although his impending grid penalty meant his strong qualifying position would not translate directly into Sunday's starting order. For Q3, Russell was given assistance by his Mercedes team mate, with Antonelli providing a slipstream that helped the Briton to set the pace after the opening runs. Russell's 1m21.929s put him narrowly ahead of Piastri and Gasly, with Leclerc leading the Ferraris in fourth. But the decisive final attempts transformed the picture. Piastri ran wide at the first chicane as he began his final lap, while Norris was unable to improve. Behind them, however, Gasly produced a superb sequence of sectors to put himself firmly in contention for pole. The Frenchman crossed the line in 1m21.786s, jumping both Piastri and Russell to claim a sensational maiden pole position. Gasly's achievement came six years after his breakthrough Formula 1 victory at the same venue, adding another remarkable chapter to his history at the Temple of Speed. Russell had to settle for second despite improving on his final effort, while Piastri completed the top three. Leclerc and Hamilton gave Ferrari fourth and fifth on home soil, ahead of Verstappen in sixth. items.article_search_text: Monza, Sep 5 (IANS) Pierre Gasly secured his maiden Formula 1 pole position in a thrilling qualifying session at the Italian Grand Prix, edging Mercedes' George Russell and McLaren's Oscar Piastri to the top spot at the Autodromo Nazionale Monza. In Q3, the Alpine driver managed a remarkable last lap of 1:21.786, overtaking Russell and Piastri to secure his first pole position in Formula 1. The achievement came after Gasly, who won his first F1 race at Monza in 2020, had been running close to the front during the entire Saturday qualifying session. Gasly was in third place, behind Russell and Piastri, after the first Q3 laps, but the Frenchman held back his best until the end. The effort he made on the last lap brought him to the top of the timing sheets and had a big effect throughout the paddock. The report also showed the effect of Alpine's newly updated car, which was powered by a Mercedes engine, enabling Gasly to perform well at the high-speed Temple of Speed. Russell came in second place, with Piastri finishing in the top three. Although Ferrari's good performance in practice did not carry over into a chance of securing pole position, Charles Leclerc managed to qualify in fourth place and Lewis Hamilton in fifth. Max Verstappen came sixth for Red Bull, while the home favourite Kimi Antonelli obtained seventh place in the other Mercedes before receiving his engine penalty. Franco Colapinto thus reached two Alpines in the top ten by securing the eighth position, beating both Lando Norris of McLaren and Arvid Lindblad of Racing Bulls. Norris, just as his teammate Piastri did, had difficulty with his brakes during qualifying. Hamilton just managed to progress through Q2 and earned his spot in Q3 by the smallest of margins. Gabriel Bortoleto of Audi was only one thousandth of a second slower in their last Q2 laps and will therefore start in 11th position, placing him in front of Ollie Bearman, who is driving the upgraded Haas-Ferrari and ahead of his Audi teammate Nico Hulkenberg. Liam Lawson, who is likewise suffering from a grid drop due to having changed his power unit, ended up in 14th place after being obstructed by Piastri on his last lap in Q2, a situation which the stewards recorded. During his second weekend acting as a Racing Bulls driver, Yuki Tsunoda suffered a setback by failing at the first qualifying jump and ended up in 17th place, while Lindblad progressed all the way to 10th position. Alexander Albon, who was also being penalised for an engine problem, assisted his Williams teammate Carlos Sainz by giving him a tow in Q1, but ended up in 18th place. He finished ahead of only the Cadillac drivers Valtteri Bottas and Sergio Perez, as well as the Aston Martin drivers Fernando Alonso and Lance Stroll. items.article_search_text: The stewards have issued Oscar Piastri a three-place grid drop for impeding Liam Lawson during qualifying for the Italian Grand Prix. 5th September 2026, 17:27 5th September 2026, 17:33 | Written by Keith Collantine Advert | Become a Supporter & go ad-free Piastri originally qualified third on the grid but will now start from sixth place. Charles Leclerc will take third place on the grid, followed by Lewis Hamilton and Max Verstappen. The stewards ruled Piastri did not intend to delay Lawson but did impeded him at the Rettifilo chicane. The incident occured after Piastri left the pits as the two Red Bull cars overtook him. Max Verstappen narrowly made it past without being held up but Piastri was unable to avoid getting in Lawson’s way. “On leaving the pits, the driver of car 81 [Piastri] was advised [by his race engineer] ‘Verstappen, Lawson and Sainz just crossing, Sainz has pitted, just Verstappen and Lawson, watch out for them as you join’. The driver of car 81 stated that he was not alerted to the fact that [Verstappen] and [Lawson] were on push laps but realised as he was almost at turn one that Verstappen was on a push lap. He slowed significantly and kept to the right to allow Verstappen to pass but was unable to do anything to avoid impeding Lawson who was close behind. “The stewards accept that with the information he had, and the situation he was placed in, the driver of car 81 had, at this stage, no other options available and hence, inadvertently, and also unnecessarily, impeded car 30 [Lawson].” Piastri previously received a penalty for impeding Nico Hulkenberg during final practice at the Japanese Grand Prix earlier this year. items.article_search_text: Pierre Gasly claimed his first pole position at Monza, denying George Russell by six hundredths of a second. 5th September 2026, 16:20 5th September 2026, 16:36 | Written by Keith Collantine Pierre Gasly will start the Italian Grand Prix from pole position after beating George Russell by six hundredths of a second in qualifying. Advert | Become a Supporter & go ad-free The Alpine driver was in contention for the quickest time throughout qualifying. Just over 24 hours since he learned he had lost his podium finish in the Monaco Grand Prix, and at the same track where he scored his only Formula 1 victory six years ago, Gasly claimed his first pole position and the first for his team in their current guide. The first runs in Q3 left four different cars separated by less than a tenth of a second: Russell, who gained a tow from team mate Andrea Kimi Antonelli approaching turn one, Oscar Piastri, Gasly and Charles Leclerc. Hamilton in the other Ferrari found himself without a tow and was seven-tenths of a second slower than his team mate. McLaren’s hopes of strengthening their position on their final runs faded when Piastri went off at the first corner. He secured third on the grid but his team mate Lando Norris running behind him was unable to improve and wound up a lowly ninth. Russell appeared to have secured pole until Gasly nabbed it off him. He had also set the quickest time earlier in the session in Q1, though team mate Franco Colapinto had to settle for eighth place. Hamilton improved to claim fifth ahead of a frustrated Max Verstappen . The Red Bull driver said his car degraded throughout the session. The pace of the Alpines created a headache for several teams, notably Ferrari, who were fortunate to get both their cars through into Q3. Gabriel Bortoleto came within a thousandth of a second of beating Hamilton into the top 10 shoot-out and Charles Leclerc was only seven-thousandths faster than his team mate. Advert | Become a RaceFans supporter and go ad-free A frustrated Liam Lawson missed Q3 after being held up by Piastri at the Rettifilo chicane on his final lap. But Lawson didn’t just direct his frustration at the McLaren driver: he also described his team’s tactics as “appalling”, saying they “left me out to dry”. The stewards will investigate the Piastri incident after qualifying. Oliver Bearman split the Audis in his upgraded Haas. Lawson came next, followed by Carlos Sainz Jnr and the other Haas of Esteban Ocon. Yuki Tsunoda failed to make the cut for Q2 in his second appearance for Racing Bulls this year. Alexander Albon, who will take a power unit change penalty, also dropped out in the first round after giving his team mate a tow. The Aston Martins were slowest of all behind the Cadillacs. Motorsport Week is an independent, FIA accredited motorsport website delivering the latest Formula 1, Formula E, GP2, GP3, WEC, IndyCar, Nascar, Formula 3, WRC, WRX, DTM, IMSA and MotoGP news and results. Oscar Piastri has detailed why he has struggled for pace in 2026 ahead of the Formula 1 Italian Grand Prix , with his last victory now a full year ago. Piastri has endured a challenging 2026, failing to win a race, while teammate and reigning world champion Lando Norris has secured two victories. The Australian's season is in stark contrast to 2025, when he mounted a championship bid and remained in the running until the final round. His performances have been inconsistent this year, securing two podiums in the opening three races but has yet to return to the rostrum. Zandvoort proved to be another challenging weekend, watching on as Norris took a second consecutive victory while Piastri finished sixth, over thirty seconds behind his teammate. Ahead of the weekend's action in. Monza, Piastri elaborated on his pace struggles, stating he wanted answers. "Yes, I think we have. I think it's not kind of the one problem that keeps recurring; it's kind of like always chasing something a little bit different, and we need to try and find it a bit quicker, both myself and the team around me, Piastri said to media, including Motorsport Week when asked if he had pinpointed the problem. "The positive from Zandvoort was that the qualifying at least looked significantly better and back to the level it should be at, and the process we're going through is just trying to extend that to the races. Obviously, the car is quite different in a race compared to every single lap, but I feel like we've got some pretty good answers to why Zandvoort, particularly, was challenging. "We're making good progress with that. We just need time and some experimentation to find some things that are going to make us quicker. But I'm confident that we're finding the right answers and finding a way forward. "It is not as straightforward as: 'It's just low grip.' I think this year, in particular, how I naturally like to drive a car is not necessarily the best way to drive these cars, and sometimes it has been, sometimes it's not, and I think that's going to be a little bit of the challenge. Oscar Piastri has endured a challenging season Different issues compounding problem for Oscar Piastri? Piastri admitted that is not just one issue causing his problems, with a narrow operating window of the MCL40 compounding his quest to turn the tide on his lack of pace. "It's not been the same issue that we've run into every time and I think for me, it's just about trying to find that right direction, the things that make this car work, and at points we've been able to find it. "At other points, we've tried a lot and not been able to find it. So it's not as simple as that. But when you're comfortable in the car, everything just becomes much easier. "It's very easy to have a spiral in both directions, both a positive spiral where things feel comfortable; you've got more capacity to think about it. Everything becomes a bit more subconscious, and it just becomes easy, almost. "Then if things aren't comfortable, you've got to think about it a lot more. You're not driving on instinct anymore, and that's why it can quite quickly unravel. "I don't think we're at that point by any stretch of the imagination, but it's certainly not come particularly easily so far in finding solutions quickly. I think we've always kind of found solutions eventually; it's more about how we can catch things a bit quicker and adapt a bit quicker through the weekend. "There are a lot of various things. It's not as simple as just struggling with this one thing, there are a lot of things tied up." Piastri faces a difficult road back to the top step of the podium, but his determination to improve will go a long way in turning the tide.
